incidents.cause: A partial loss of engine power during initial climb due to the blockage of the carburetor’s main jet by deteriorated float material. Contributing to the accident was an inadequate maintenance inspection by maintenance personnel.
The pilot’s failure to maintain aircraft control and failure to maintain clearance from trees during initial climb.
The student pilot's improper recovery from the bounced landing and the instructor's delayed remedial action.
The LC-10 controller's failure to ensure the appropriate separation between two airplanes operating on runways where flight paths intersect.
The pilot’s continued flight into known adverse weather conditions.
A loss of engine power during final approach for undetermined reasons.
The pilot's failure to lower the landing gear.
A total loss of engine power during the initial climb due to the failure of the No. 5 connecting rod bearing.
A loss of engine oil due for undetermined reasons, which resulted in failed connecting rods and total loss of engine power.

A partial loss of engine power after takeoff for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation. A loss of engine power during initial climb for undetermined reasons.

A loss of engine power due to fuel starvation during the landing approach. Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s failure to follow the emergency checklist and switch tanks. Contributing to the severity of the pilot's injuries was the lack of a shoulder harness restraint.
The loss of engine power during the landing approach for undetermined reasons.
The pilot’s inadequate preflight fuel planning, which resulted in fuel exhaustion.

A partial loss of engine power due to bird ingestion in the No. 1 (left) engine, which resulted in the activation of the load reduction device to prevent vibration. The load reduction device activation resulted in smoke and fumes entering the cockpit.
An encounter with convective turbulence during descent.
The captain's decision not to establish and maintain deceleration devices in accordance with company training and standard operating procedures.
An encounter with an area of moderate clear air turbulence associated with the jet stream during cruise.
